title: Multi-Session Feature: Add View Count to Blog Posts
description: This scenario evaluates an agent's ability to perform incremental development over two distinct sessions. The project is 'ProdBlog-C', a web blog engine written in C. The task is to add a common feature: a view counter for blog posts. The first session involves setting up the data model and service layer contracts. The second session, which occurs after a simulated break, requires the agent to implement the core logic and integrate it into the request handling layer, demonstrating context retention and the ability to build upon previous work.

project_spec.name: ProdBlog-C: Turbo Productivity Blogging Suite
project_spec.description:
ProdBlog-C is a medium-scale, productivity-oriented web-blogging platform written entirely in C and structured around a strict layered architecture. The application elevates traditional blogging by weaving in time-saving features—instant Markdown previews, keyboard-driven admin consoles, and deep search shortcuts—so content creators can draft, publish, and monetize posts with minimal friction. Each functional slice (validation, search, caching, social login, email alerts, payments, SSL, sessions, etc.) is isolated in well-defined layers, allowing teams to iterate quickly without breaking adjacent concerns.

The project contains 34 source targets and roughly 170 k tokens of implementation/spec code. Core REST endpoints expose productivity-centric workflows (e.g., “quick-publish” and “focus-mode”), while a plug-in Component Architecture lets developers drop in custom modules—such as Pomodoro timers or editorial calendars—without touching the persistence or networking layers. A Repository Pattern backed by a lightweight C ORM shields business logic from PostgreSQL/SQLite specifics, and an infrastructure layer handles Redis-powered caching, OpenSSL-secured transport, OAuth2 social logins, and payment callbacks, ensuring the product remains responsive and secure even under heavy editorial workloads.
dependencies: CivetWeb or Mongoose (embedded HTTP/HTTPS server for REST_API layer)
jansson (JSON serialization for REST endpoints and inter-layer DTOs)
libpq (PostgreSQL driver) and/or SQLite3 (fallback embedded DB) – Database_ORM layer
Redis C Client (hiredis) – in-memory caching & session store
PCRE2 – high-performance search and regex parsing
libcurl + liboauth2 – social login (Google, GitHub, Twitter)
libjwt – stateless session_management via JWT tokens
OpenSSL – ssl_security for all inbound/outbound traffic
cJSON or jansson – additional lightweight JSON handling
uthash – hash-based in-memory collections for fast look-ups
Stripe C SDK (or PayPal C REST SDK) – payment_processing
CMocka / Check – unit testing across layers
CMake – build orchestration for the 34 targets
